generator.note: K/P values below are exact deterministic graph computations, not wall-clock samples; every row is reproduced by an assertion in the referenced test file.

Revised after review: a strict_public_api_surface contract's assemblies list is schema-unbounded, so one api_snapshot is not provably owned by exactly one project; falls back to full scope until a deterministic contract-to-assemblies-to-projects mapping exists.

change_to_project_ownership_resolution_g.note: Added after review: every row above and every ChangedInput in the test suite supplies OwningProjectIds directly; this task never derives 'which project(s) own this changed path' from the path itself. For the synthetic corpus the test author already knows the answer because BenchmarkWorkloadGenerator produced the path deterministically, which is circular as evidence for the general mapping question.
change_to_project_ownership_resolution_g.authoritative_basis: MSBuild evaluated project items (@(Compile) after glob expansion), including <Compile Include="..." Link="..." /> for linked/shared files that live outside the owning project's own directory, plus the Directory.Build.props/Import chain that contributed to that evaluation.
change_to_project_ownership_resolution_g.why_path_prefix_matching_is_insufficient: A file's location on disk is not proof of which project(s) compile it. tools/scripts/classify_pr_traffic_mix.py's path-pattern classifier is explicitly informal/approximate for exactly this reason and is not a substitute for MSBuild evaluation.

evaluator_family_scope_by_family.note: Added after review, then revised after two further review passes: the reference-graph dependents closure above is not one safe superset for every contract family, and neither is 'the changed project alone'. These rows are grounded in the actual checkers under src/ArchLinterNet.Core/Execution/, not assumed, and are asserted by EvaluatorFamilies_RequireDifferentScopesThanTheGenericDependentsClosure. This is a representative five-family subset (four contract-family groups, with coverage split in two) of the roughly 35 named contract families in schema/dependencies.arch.schema.json, not exhaustive coverage. The schema's root strict/audit arrays also map to the base dependency family, which the exhaustive disposition test now includes and conservatively falls back to full population.

families.checker_evidence: LayerChecker/ExternalDependencyChecker/AllowOnlyChecker scan only the changed project's own layer's own outgoing references, but ArchitectureNamespaceViolationFinder.MatchReference classifies the referenced TARGET type; a change to the target project can flip an unchanged dependent's verdict, so the safe bound is the dependents closure, not the changed project alone.
families.revision_note: First correction claimed required_k=1 (strictly-narrower); that was itself wrong and is corrected here.

families.checker_evidence: CycleChecker builds one shared inter-layer edge graph across every layer named by the contract and runs global cycle detection once over it; even the dependents closure is not a safe bound.
PublicApiSurfaceChecker scopes to assemblies explicitly co-listed in one contract's assemblies field, a membership relationship not modeled by the project-reference graph.

CheckProjectCoverageContract/CheckAssemblyCoverageContract classify each item independently from only that item's own namespaces against policy-declared layers, never another project's code, and each item is by construction exactly one project or one assembly; current execution re-scans the whole solution and aggregates into one findings list per run.

ArchitectureCoverageInventory.Build groups the whole solution's types by namespace string and picks one representative type, so a shared namespace entry can span multiple projects; ArchitectureDependencyEdgeCoverageService.Check evaluates declared layer-pairs against edges observed across the whole coverage inventory; ArchitectureSemanticCoverageService.BuildSummary iterates every type via the shared role catalog (same unproven cross-project classification risk as ReferenceGraphLocal); rule_input is policy-level, not project-scoped.
families.revision_note: First correction lumped all of 'coverage' into AggregatedGlobalScan at required_k=1. Second correction moved dependency_edge/semantic_role/rule_input out but still left namespace grouped with project/assembly at required_k=1 -- that was itself wrong, since only project and assembly are inherently single-project/assembly by construction; namespace is moved here in this revision.

base_dependency_family_fallback.reason: The base dependencyContract arrays are represented explicitly in schema enumeration but do not yet have a checker-grounded narrower invalidation rule.

evaluator_family_scope_by_family.unanalyzed_families_default: full-population-fallback (safe widening; not claimed safe by any model here)

repository_pr_traffic_mix.method: path-pattern classification of file lists from the last N commits on this repository's own main history; approximate, not a literal application of ChangedProjectScopePlanner (which requires structured project/edge graph input the raw commit history does not provide)
repository_pr_traffic_mix.reproduce_command: uv run --project tools/pyproject.toml python tools/scripts/classify_pr_traffic_mix.py --end-ref bb533f0f2fc0d2e30addc7a4110adda26e825e68 --commit-count 300
repository_pr_traffic_mix.predicate_correction_note: Corrected after review: the classifier originally counted ANY file under src/ or tests/ as project-source regardless of extension, folding non-compiled files (JSON fixtures, README, .resx, etc.) into this bucket and overstating it at 18/300 (0.06). project-source now requires a .cs extension specifically; non-.cs files under src/tests classify separately as non-source-file-under-src-or-tests.
repository_pr_traffic_mix.caveat: The remaining ~85% mix project-source with docs/openspec/non-source-file-under-src-or-tests/other paths not classified here; whether those other paths are architecture-lint-relevant at all is a separate, unanswered mapping question this task surfaces but does not resolve.

timing_evidence.scope: Staged synthetic #502 workloads, strict analysis-profile/v1 phases, sequential max-parallelism=1. Fixed phases are policy composition/configuration/policy consistency; project-dependent work is the remaining non-output top-level phase time.
timing_evidence.authority_limit: Modeled K/P estimates are not advisory execution evidence and cannot establish preview/execution equivalence.

p0_gate.constraint: No incremental-analysis implementation child issue may be created from this evidence based solely on the current (pre-normalization) dogfood latency table in #991. Re-evaluation against normalized consumer CI is required first.
p0_gate.action_taken_in_this_task: Outcome C recorded and no implementation child issue created because the correctness boundary remains unsafe: ownership fixtures establish the evaluated Compile-item basis but there is no production changed-path planner, only a few family scopes have a narrower reviewed disposition, and preview/execution coverage is unproven. The timing artifact is descriptive full-strict evidence with modeled K/P effects; no percentage threshold was used. Re-evaluate only after #991 reaches its decision gate and normalized consumer evidence plus issue-specific implementation/trust costs can support a decision.
